label: input token i during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter i. It fires on every original-phase step whose input is i (rate about 100%, dev F1 0.998, precision 1.0) and never on any other input token. It is silent on the <DEL> step and on nearly all copy-phase steps where i is fed back as input (only about 350 weak copy-phase activations, at recall_idx 1). Magnitude is highest (near max 2.98) when i is the first original token. From the examples it is lower when i appears later in the sequence (about 0.6-0.9 of max) and lower again for repeated occurrences of i (about 0.3-0.8 of max); I only checked those two effects against the examples, not quantitatively.

issues: Core predicate holds up on test: precision 1.000, recall 0.997, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9998, correlation 0.96. There are 0 false positives on test.

The misses are one systematic class, but a negligible one: 343 test steps carry 0.0% of the activation mass. They are all weak copy-phase activations (0.01-0.07 of max) at recall_idx 1 when the input is the fed-back i, and they occur when i was original token 0. The explanation already describes this correctly. The predicate (in_tok==i)&(phase==2) scores F1 0.003, which confirms the feature is essentially silent in the copy phase.

The magnitude-versus-position claim is understated. The activation mass share per active step falls steadily with t: relative to t=0 it is about 0.71x at t=4 and about 0.24x at t=8. On test, original-phase i at t>=7 holds 7.7% of active steps but only 3.0% of the mass, so the mean is about 0.3 of max. The explanation's '0.6-0.9 of max later in the sequence' is too high for late positions; it should say the magnitude falls roughly monotonically with position, to about 0.25-0.4 of max at t=7-8.

The repeat-occurrence effect is confirmed in direction: repeated occurrences (in_first=0) have about 0.74x the mean magnitude of first occurrences. There is also a mild unreported modulation: activation rate and mass decrease as n_digits rises. Both are magnitude details only and do not affect the label.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
